claim: For every integer n >= exp(exp(Y)) there is a prime p with n^3 + 1/2 < p <= n^3 + 3n^2 + 1/2, hence between n^3 and (n+1)^3
X0: 3*exp(Y)  (lower bound for X = log x, x = n^3 + 1/2)

sources.I1: Cully-Hugill, J. Number Theory 247 (2023), arXiv:2107.14468, Theorem 2 and Table 2 (K = 2.4798 for log x >= 1e6)
